paragraphs.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃

i18n.en: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

paragraphs.text: קַדֶּשׁ־לִ֨י כָל־בְּכ֜וֹר פֶּ֤טֶר כָּל־רֶ֙חֶם֙ בִּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בָּאָדָ֖ם וּבַבְּהֵמָ֑ה לִ֖י הֽוּא׃

i18n.en: "Consecrate to me every firstborn, the first issue of every womb among the children of Yisra'el, among humans and among animals; it is mine."

notes.official: The firstborn-consecration command *qaddeš-lî ḵol-bĕḵôr peṭer kol-reḥem* 'consecrate to me every firstborn, the first issue of every womb' establishes the cultic-institutional framework of the firstborn-redemption. See the central entry `pesach-pidyon-firstborn-passover-firstborn-redemption-cross-corpus` for the cross-corpus reach to Num 3, 18 and the NT Luke 2:22-24 Mary-and-Joseph-presentation pericope.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶל־הָעָ֗ם זָכ֞וֹר אֶת־הַיּ֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְצָאתֶ֤ם מִמִּצְרַ֙יִם֙ מִבֵּ֣ית עֲבָדִ֔ים כִּ֚י בְּחֹ֣זֶק יָ֔ד הוֹצִ֧יא יְהֹוָ֛ה אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִזֶּ֑ה וְלֹ֥א יֵאָכֵ֖ל חָמֵֽץ׃

i18n.en: And Moses said to the people, "Remember this day on which you went out from Mitsrayim, from the house of slaves, for with a mighty hand YHWH brought you out from this place; no leavened bread shall be eaten.

paragraphs.text: הַיּ֖וֹם אַתֶּ֣ם יֹצְאִ֑ים בְּחֹ֖דֶשׁ הָאָבִֽיב׃

i18n.en: Today you are going out, in the month of Aviv.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֣ה כִֽי־יְבִֽיאֲךָ֣ יְהוָ֡ה אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ הַֽ֠כְּנַעֲנִי וְהַחִתִּ֨י וְהָאֱמֹרִ֜י וְהַחִוִּ֣י וְהַיְבוּסִ֗י אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִשְׁבַּ֤ע לַאֲבֹתֶ֙יךָ֙ לָ֣תֶת לָ֔ךְ אֶ֛רֶץ זָבַ֥ת חָלָ֖ב וּדְבָ֑שׁ וְעָבַדְתָּ֛ אֶת־הָעֲבֹדָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את בַּחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: And it shall be, when YHWH brings you into the land of the Canaanite and the Hittite and the Amorite and the Hivite and the Jebusite, which he swore to your fathers to give you, a land flowing with milk and honey, that you shall perform this service in this month.

paragraphs.text: שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים תֹּאכַ֣ל מַצֹּ֑ת וּבַיּוֹם֙ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י חַ֖ג לַיהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there shall be a festival to YHWH.

paragraphs.text: מַצּוֹת֙ יֵֽאָכֵ֔ל אֵ֖ת שִׁבְעַ֣ת הַיָּמִ֑ים וְלֹֽא־יֵרָאֶ֨ה לְךָ֜ חָמֵ֗ץ וְלֹֽא־יֵרָאֶ֥ה לְךָ֛ שְׂאֹ֖ר בְּכָל־גְּבֻלֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: Unleavened bread shall be eaten for the seven days; and no leavened bread shall be seen with you, and no leaven shall be seen with you within all your territory.

paragraphs.text: וְהִגַּדְתָּ֣ לְבִנְךָ֔ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא לֵאמֹ֑ר בַּעֲב֣וּר זֶ֗ה עָשָׂ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לִ֔י בְּצֵאתִ֖י מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And you shall tell your son on that day, saying, 'Because of this YHWH acted for me when I went out from Mitsrayim.'

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָה֩ לְךָ֨ לְא֜וֹת עַל־יָדְךָ֗ וּלְזִכָּרוֹן֙ בֵּ֣ין עֵינֶ֔יךָ לְמַ֗עַן תִּהְיֶ֛ה תּוֹרַ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה בְּפִ֑יךָ כִּ֚י בְּיָ֣ד חֲזָקָ֔ה הוֹצִֽאֲךָ֥ יְהֹוָ֖ה מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And it shall be for you as a sign on your hand and as a memorial between your eyes, in order that the torah of YHWH may be in your mouth; for with a mighty hand YHWH brought you out from Mitsrayim.

notes.official: The 'sign on your hand and memorial between your eyes' formulation is the Pentateuchal prooftext for the rabbinic tefillin (phylactery) tradition; cf. Deut 6:8, 11:18. The Karaite reading takes the language metaphorically; the rabbinic-Pharisaic tradition takes it literally as the physical-tefillin-binding institution. The dispute is documented in the apparatus.

paragraphs.text: וְשָׁמַרְתָּ֛ אֶת־הַחֻקָּ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את לְמוֹעֲדָ֑הּ מִיָּמִ֖ים יָמִֽימָה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And you shall keep this statute at its appointed season, from year to year.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֞ה כִּֽי־יְבִֽאֲךָ֤ יְהוָה֙ אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר נִשְׁבַּ֥ע לְךָ֖ וְלַֽאֲבֹתֶ֑יךָ וּנְתָנָ֖הּ לָֽךְ׃

i18n.en: And it shall be, when YHWH brings you to the land of the Canaanite, as he swore to you and to your fathers, and gives it to you,

paragraphs.text: וְהַעֲבַרְתָּ֥ כָל־פֶּֽטֶר־רֶ֖חֶם לַֽיהֹוָ֑ה וְכָל־פֶּ֣טֶר ׀ שֶׁ֣גֶר בְּהֵמָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִהְיֶ֥ה לְךָ֛ הַזְּכָרִ֖ים לַיהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: that you shall set apart for YHWH every first issue of the womb; and every firstling that is dropped from an animal which you have, the males shall be YHWH's.

notes.official: The set-apart-for-YHWH protocol for the *peṭer-reḥem* firstborns continues the v-2 firstborn-consecration institution. See the central entry.

paragraphs.text: וְכָל־פֶּ֤טֶר חֲמֹר֙ תִּפְדֶּ֣ה בְשֶׂ֔ה וְאִם־לֹ֥א תִפְדֶּ֖ה וַעֲרַפְתּ֑וֹ וְכֹ֨ל בְּכ֥וֹר אָדָ֛ם בְּבָנֶ֖יךָ תִּפְדֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: And every firstling of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb; and if you do not redeem it, you shall break its neck. And every firstborn of a human among your sons you shall redeem.

notes.official: The donkey-firstborn-redeemed-with-a-lamb protocol; cross-corpus to Num 18:15-16, Lev 27:27. The human-firstborn-redemption obligation establishes the foundation for the post-biblical *pidyon ha-ben* ceremony.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֞ה כִּֽי־יִשְׁאָלְךָ֥ בִנְךָ֛ מָחָ֖ר לֵאמֹ֣ר מַה־זֹּ֑את וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֔יו בְּחֹ֣זֶק יָ֗ד הוֹצִיאָ֧נוּ יְהוָ֛ה מִמִּצְרַ֖יִם מִבֵּ֥ית עֲבָדִֽים׃

i18n.en: And it shall be, when your son asks you in time to come, saying, 'What is this?' then you shall say to him, 'By a mighty hand YHWH brought us out from Mitsrayim, from the house of slaves.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֗י כִּֽי־הִקְשָׁ֣ה פַרְעֹה֮ לְשַׁלְּחֵנוּ֒ וַיַּהֲרֹ֨ג יְהֹוָ֤ה כָּל־בְּכוֹר֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם מִבְּכֹ֥ר אָדָ֖ם וְעַד־בְּכ֣וֹר בְּהֵמָ֑ה עַל־כֵּן֩ אֲנִ֨י זֹבֵ֜חַ לַֽיהוָ֗ה כָּל־פֶּ֤טֶר רֶ֙חֶם֙ הַזְּכָרִ֔ים וְכָל־בְּכ֥וֹר בָּנַ֖י אֶפְדֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when Pharaoh hardened himself against sending us out, that YHWH killed every firstborn in the land of Mitsrayim, from the firstborn of human to the firstborn of animal. Therefore I sacrifice to YHWH every male that opens the womb, but every firstborn of my sons I redeem.'

notes.official: The Pharaoh-hardening recapitulation *hiqšâ par'ōh lĕ-šallĕḥēnû* deploys the *qšh* 'to be hard, severe' root (cf. Ex 7:3); see the central entry `hardening-of-pharaoh-heart-quishah-lev-ex-7-14-divine-action-theological-problem-cross-corpus` for the mixed-agency theological pattern across Ex 4-14.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֤ה לְאוֹת֙ עַל־יָ֣דְכָ֔ה וּלְטוֹטָפֹ֖ת בֵּ֣ין עֵינֶ֑יךָ כִּ֚י בְּחֹ֣זֶק יָ֔ד הוֹצִיאָ֥נוּ יְהוָ֖ה מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And it shall be for a sign on your hand and as frontlets between your eyes, for with a mighty hand YHWH brought us out from Mitsrayim."

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֗י בְּשַׁלַּ֣ח פַּרְעֹה֮ אֶת־הָעָם֒ וְלֹא־נָחָ֣ם אֱלֹהִ֗ים דֶּ֚רֶךְ אֶ֣רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים כִּ֥י קָר֖וֹב ה֑וּא כִּ֣י ׀ אָמַ֣ר אֱלֹהִ֗ים פֶּֽן־יִנָּחֵ֥ם הָעָ֛ם בִּרְאֹתָ֥ם מִלְחָמָ֖ה וְשָׁ֥בוּ מִצְרָֽיְמָה׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when Pharaoh sent the people out, that the Elohim did not lead them by the way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near; for the Elohim said, "Lest the people change their mind when they see war and return to Mitsrayim."

notes.official: The divine-routing-detour decision — Israel led not via the Philistine coastal route (the 'Way of Horus' / *via maris*, the shortest route) but via the wilderness-of-the-Reed-Sea route. The Egyptological-historical scholarship (Hoffmeier 2005) documents the Philistine-route as a heavily-fortified Egyptian military corridor in the New Kingdom period, supporting the narrative's strategic rationale.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּסֵּ֨ב אֱלֹהִ֧ים ׀ אֶת־הָעָ֛ם דֶּ֥רֶךְ הַמִּדְבָּ֖ר יַם־ס֑וּף וַחֲמֻשִׁ֛ים עָל֥וּ בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: So the Elohim led the people around by way of the wilderness, the Sea of Reeds; and the children of Yisra'el went up armed for battle out of the land of Mitsrayim.

notes.official: The *yam-sûp̄* designation — 'Sea of Reeds' on the philological-modern-critical convention; the LXX-Vulgate-KJV 'Red Sea' tradition is documented at the central entry `yam-suf-sea-of-reeds-vs-red-sea-geographical-textual-cross-corpus`. The *ḥămušîm* hapax — preserved as 'armed for battle' per the dominant English-translation tradition, with the LXX 'in five divisions' / Cassuto 'by fifties' / midrashic 'eagerly' alternatives documented at the overlay entry.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקַּ֥ח מֹשֶׁ֛ה אֶת־עַצְמ֥וֹת יוֹסֵ֖ף עִמּ֑וֹ כִּי֩ הַשְׁבֵּ֨עַ הִשְׁבִּ֜יעַ אֶת־בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר פָּקֹ֨ד יִפְקֹ֤ד אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶתְכֶ֔ם וְהַעֲלִיתֶ֧ם אֶת־עַצְמֹתַ֛י מִזֶּ֖ה אִתְּכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And Moses took the bones of Yosef with him; for he had solemnly sworn the children of Yisra'el, saying, "The Elohim will surely visit you, and you shall carry up my bones from here with you."

notes.official: The Joseph-bones forward-bridge (Gen 50:24-25 → Ex 13:19 → Josh 24:32) is the Pentateuchal-Joshua narrative-thread that the WoH-Translation preserves; see the existing entries `paqod-yiphqod-divine-visitation-exodus-formula-cross-corpus` and `atzmot-yosef-bones-for-exodus-narrative-forward-bridge-cross-corpus`.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִסֻּכֹּ֑ת וַיַּחֲנ֣וּ בְאֵתָ֔ם בִּקְצֵ֖ה הַמִּדְבָּֽר׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Sukkot and camped at Etam, at the edge of the wilderness.

paragraphs.text: וַֽיהוָ֡ה הֹלֵךְ֩ לִפְנֵיהֶ֨ם יוֹמָ֜ם בְּעַמּ֤וּד עָנָן֙ לַנְחֹתָ֣ם הַדֶּ֔רֶךְ וְלַ֛יְלָה בְּעַמּ֥וּד אֵ֖שׁ לְהָאִ֣יר לָהֶ֑ם לָלֶ֖כֶת יוֹמָ֥ם וָלָֽיְלָה׃

i18n.en: And YHWH went before them by day in a pillar of cloud to lead them on the way, and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light, so that they could travel by day and by night.

notes.official: **THE PILLAR OF CLOUD AND FIRE introduction-site.** The *ʿammûd ʿānān* by day / *ʿammûd ʾēš* by night is the Hebrew Bible's central divine-presence-by-locomotion marker. See the central entry `pillar-of-cloud-and-fire-ammud-ha-anan-ve-esh-divine-presence-marker-cross-corpus` for the full cross-corpus reach (Ex 14, Ex 33, Ex 40, Num 9, Deut 31, Neh 9, Ps 78, 105; Isa 4:5 the eschatological reactivation; 1 Cor 10:1-2, Heb 12 the NT typological appropriations) and the operational disavowals against (i) the Raëlian-canon 'Elohim-craft visual marker / spacecraft navigation system' reading (acknowledgment-without-endorsement per the Shi'ur Qomah parasangs precedent and the Qur'an *inshiqāq al-qamar* precedent), (ii) the Sitchin 'Anunnaki-aerial-vehicle' reading, (iii) the Christian-typology 'pillar = preincarnate Christ' reading, (iv) the naturalistic-reduction to 'volcanic plume' or 'incense-brazier' explanation.

paragraphs.text: לֹֽא־יָמִ֞ישׁ עַמּ֤וּד הֶֽעָנָן֙ יוֹמָ֔ם וְעַמּ֥וּד הָאֵ֖שׁ לָ֑יְלָה לִפְנֵ֖י הָעָֽם׃ (פ)

i18n.en: The pillar of cloud did not depart by day, nor the pillar of fire by night, from before the people.

notes.official: The continuous-presence of the pillar; the *lōʾ yāmîš* 'did not depart' establishes the never-interrupted divine-presence-marker tradition that recurs at Ex 14:19-20, 14:24, 33:9-10, 40:34-38, Num 9:15-23.
